title: Small representatives of bounded coherent cocones
statement: Use the nested universes, smallness and $\kappa$-small simplicial sets of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and the quasicategories, coherent cocones and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal and let $C$ be a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory. There is a $\mathcal U$-small family of triples $(K_r,a_r,\lambda_r)$, where $K_r$ is a $\kappa$-small simplicial set, $a_r\in C$, and $\lambda_r:p_r\to\Delta_{K_r}a_r$ is a coherent cocone in $C$, with the following property. For every $\kappa$-small simplicial set $K$ and every coherent cocone $\lambda:p\to\Delta_Ka$ in $C$, there exist $r$ and an isomorphism of simplicial sets $u:K_r\cong K$ such that $a_r=a$ and $\lambda_r=u^*\lambda$ as coherent cocone data (so $p_r=pu$). The subfamily of colimiting cocones is small and represents every colimiting cocone in this same sense. Empty bases are included. No existence of colimits in $C$ is assumed.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.3.6.2, proof, printed p. 413, smallness reduction for the collection R; Definition 5.3.6.5 and Example 5.3.6.8, p. 415, use all bounded colimiting cocones. The bounded-shape counting argument needed here is stated separately, not asserted to be the verbatim proposition. Agent-formulated auxiliary consequence; read the April 9, 2017 HTT text online. Not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text: Let $N(K)$ denote the disjoint union of the nondegenerate simplices of $K$, with their dimensions. By the definition of $\kappa$-smallness choose an injection $j:N(K)\hookrightarrow\kappa$. The nondegenerate decomposition gives each $x\in K_n$ a unique pair $(y,\sigma)$, with $y$ nondegenerate of dimension $r$ and $\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$, such that $x=K(\sigma)y$. The set of triples $(n,r,\sigma)$ is countable: for fixed $n,r$ it consists of finitely many maps between finite sets, and the pairs $(n,r)$ are countable. Choose a numerical encoding $e(n,r,\sigma)$. Thus $(n,x)\mapsto(j(y),e(n,r,\sigma))$ embeds $\coprod_nK_n$ into the fixed small set $A=\kappa\times\mathbb N$. This bound is by a small set, not a claim that all simplices number less than $\kappa$; it works also for $\kappa=\aleph_0$.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets; elementary encoding consequence of the nondegenerate decomposition

proof.text: Form the set $B$ of all simplicial structures whose degree-$n$ sets $L_n$ are subsets of $A$ and which have fewer than $\kappa$ nondegenerate simplices. This is a small set: the carriers are elements of $\prod_{n\in\mathbb N}\mathcal P(A)$, and all operator graphs are elements of $\prod_{\alpha\in\operatorname{Mor}(\Delta)}\mathcal P(A\times A)$; the source/target, identity and composition equations and the cardinal condition merely select a subset. These products, powersets and their subsets belong to the Grothendieck universe $\mathcal U$, since $A$ and the countable object and arrow sets of $\Delta$ do. For any $K$ in the question, restrict the embedding of step 1 to bijections $b_n:K_n\to L_n\subseteq A$, and define $L(\alpha)=b_mK(\alpha)b_n^{-1}$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. Substitution proves the functor equations and shows $u_n=b_n^{-1}$ defines a simplicial isomorphism $u:L\cong K$. An invertible simplicial map preserves degeneracy in both directions by commuting with all simplex operators. Therefore $L\in B$.

source.place: Auxiliary descendant size argument for paragraph 2; agent-written explicit carrier/operator encoding, expanding the small collection of diagrams in HTT Proposition 5.3.6.2, proof, p. 413

proof.text: For each $L\in B$ take all pairs $(a,H)$ with $a\in C_0$ and $H:L\times\Delta^1\to C$ a simplicial map whose restriction at $1$ is constant at $a$. Put $p=H|_{L\times\{0\}}$ and regard $H$ as the coherent cocone $p\to\Delta_La$. This uses exactly the internal-functor definition of coherent transformation. There are a small set of these pairs: simplicial maps form a subset of $\prod_{n\geq0}\operatorname{Maps}(L_n\times(\Delta^1)_n,C_n)$, and $C_0$, all factors and the countable product belong to $\mathcal U$. The disjoint union of these sets over the small set $B$ is a small index set $R$. Its triples $(L,a,H)$ are the required family; retaining all pairs avoids any choice of cocones or any colimit-existence assumption.

source.place: Auxiliary descendant size argument for paragraph 2; agent-written count of the coherent transformations defined in def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones

proof.text: Given $(K,a,\lambda)$ choose $u:L\cong K$ from step 2 and write $H:K\times\Delta^1\to C$ for its coherent transformation. The pair $(a,H\circ(u\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}))$ occurs in $R$. Its endpoint at $0$ is $pu$, and its endpoint at $1$ is the constant diagram at the very same vertex $a$. Consequently the indexed cocone equals $u^*\lambda$ as actual simplicial map data, including all higher simplices, with $a_r=a$ literally. This proves the representative property without replacing $a$ by an equivalent object.

source.place: Auxiliary descendant size argument for paragraph 2; agent-written restriction calculation for coherent transformations

proof.text: Select $R_{\mathrm{col}}\subseteq R$ by the predicate that the indexed cocone is colimiting; this subset is small. To check that it still represents every colimiting cocone, precomposition with $u\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^n}$ gives, in every degree, a simplicial isomorphism $\operatorname{Fun}(K,C)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(L,C)$, with inverse precomposition with $u^{-1}\times\mathrm{id}$. It commutes with constants and with the two endpoint maps. Apply these inverse maps to the explicit simplicial pullbacks defining the cocone categories of $p$ and $pu$: they give inverse simplicial isomorphisms, fixing the apex and sending $\lambda$ to $u^*\lambda$. For each pair of cocones they also give inverse maps on the right-pinched mapping spaces, by postcomposition on the maps from $\Delta^{n+1}$ in the definition. Hence all mapping spaces out of $\lambda$ are contractible if and only if those out of $u^*\lambda$ are; the initial-object definition of colimiting is preserved. For $K=\varnothing$ all carriers and operators in step 2 are empty, and step 3 contains the unique transformation for each separately indexed $a\in C_0$. If $C$ is empty there are no such apices and $R$ is empty. These cases require no initial object in $C$.

lean.statement: theorem small_cocone_representatives (κ : Cardinal.{u}) (hκ : κ.IsRegular) (C : SSet.{u}) [SSet.Quasicategory C] : ∃ (R : Type u) (K : R → SSet.{u}) (p : ∀ r : R, K r ⟶ C) (coc : ∀ r : R, (SSet.Enhanced.coconeCategory (p r)) _⦋0⦌), (∀ r : R, IsKappaSmall κ (K r)) ∧ (∀ (K' : SSet.{u}) (hK' : IsKappaSmall κ K') (p' : K' ⟶ C) (t' : (SSet.Enhanced.coconeCategory p') _⦋0⦌), ∃ (r : R) (u : K r ≅ K'), p r = u.hom ≫ p' ∧ (coc r).1.1 = t'.1.1 ∧ (coc r).1.2 = ((ihom Δ[1]).map ((MonoidalClosed.pre u.hom).app C)).app (op ⦋0⦌) t'.1.2) ∧ (∀ (K' : SSet.{u}) (hK' : IsKappaSmall κ K') (p' : K' ⟶ C) (t' : (SSet.Enhanced.coconeCategory p') _⦋0⦌), SSet.Enhanced.IsColimiting p' t' → ∃ (r : R) (u : K r ≅ K'), SSet.Enhanced.IsColimiting (p r) (coc r) ∧ p r = u.hom ≫ p' ∧ (coc r).1.1 = t'.1.1 ∧ (coc r).1.2 = ((ihom Δ[1]).map ((MonoidalClosed.pre u.hom).app C)).app (op ⦋0⦌) t'.1.2)
